meta.artifact: nested demand-usage, built from fetched data

tiers.T2: derived - computed from other inputs via a stated formula
tiers.T3: source_found_unverified - published figure + URL, not independently checked
tiers.T4: assumption - bounded range, Monte Carlo simulated, never an LLM magnitude

verification.finding: Re-fetched independently; byte-identical. BUT the record carries isReported=False — India did not itself report this line to Comtrade, so the figure is mirror data reconstructed from partner countries' export declarations, not Indian customs.

verification.claim: India ketchup & sauces consumption 2024: 1.2 mn t (production 1.3 mn t)
verification.finding: Page re-opened and the figure is stated verbatim, with India ranked 3rd globally behind China (3.0 mn t) and the USA (2.1 mn t). Citation corrected to the article that actually carries the number (the previously cited store page does not).

Patent RU2728363C1 states acetic acid 0.6-0.8 wt% on a 70% basis. Back-solve (x0.70 / 5% vinegar strength) gives 8.4-11.2 wt% vinegar. Arithmetic re-verified. Corroborating '7-12% w/w' figure comes from a low-quality commercial page and is treated as weak support, not a second source.

Primary page returns HTTP 403 (paywalled) — the figure could not be confirmed at source. It survives only an indirect check: 12,069.7 mn L over 1.451 bn people = 8.3 L/person, consistent with a separately reported ~9 L/person. Retained at T3, which is precisely the tag for 'published somewhere, not verified'.

FAILED as originally cited. The build used $485.08M for 2024; the IMARC page states no 2024 figure at all and gives 2025 = $455.66M. The $485.08M came from a search-result summary aggregating several vendors, not from this page. Corrected to $455.66M (2025) with the year relabelled. Confirmed: no tonnage is published anywhere on the page.

FAILED. The page carries no production tonnage at all. It does state a market value of ~$870M and that ~70% of the industry is unorganised — both confirmed. The tonnage claim came from a search summary. Host volume downgraded from T3 to T4 with a wide band.

FAILED. The page states no market size figure whatsoever — only the phrase 'recent estimates position the market in the high hundreds of millions'. The $301.6M came from a search summary and cannot be attributed to this or any verified source. The quantitative top-down cross-check has been REMOVED. What remains is a qualitative disagreement: this build gives ~$218M against unsourced language suggesting 2-4x more.

leaves.name: Aerated / carbonated soft drinks

host.source: MarketLine — India CSD consumption volume 2024 (page paywalled, HTTP 403)
host.note: AUDIT: could not be confirmed at source — the primary page returns 403. Survives only an indirect check: 12,069.7 mn L / 1.451 bn people = 8.3 L/person, consistent with a separately reported ~9 L/person. T3 is exactly the right tag for this state.

intensity.source: No numeric cap exists — FSSAI permits acetic acid (INS 260) at GMP level
intensity.note: THE REGULATORY ROUTE FAILS HERE. Acetic acid is permitted but uncapped for many categories, so no ml/L can be read off the regulation. Only a label study could resolve this.

adopt.note: Mainstream colas use phosphoric acid, citrus drinks use citric. Vinegar is rare.

price.source: Comtrade import unit value, food grade

leaves.note: The worked example from the brief. It is also the WEAKEST leaf in the build — two of three inputs are unbounded by any source. Worth seeing that the headline example is the hardest case, not the easiest.

leaves.name: Sauces, ketchup & condiments

host.source: IndexBox — India ketchup & sauces consumption 2024 (1.2 mn t)
host.note: India is the 3rd-largest consumer globally after China (3.0 mn t) and USA (2.1 mn t). Production 1.3 mn t.

intensity.source: Derived from patent RU2728363C1 formulation spec
intensity.formula: 0.6-0.8 wt% acetic acid @70% basis x 0.70 / 5% vinegar strength = 8.4-11.2 wt% vinegar
intensity.note: CROSS-CHECKED: independent formulation guidance puts vinegar at 7-12% w/w of ketchup. Two unrelated routes land on the same range — this is the strongest coefficient in the model.

adopt.source: Vinegar is near-definitional for ketchup; broader 'sauces' is mixed

price.source: Comtrade import unit value, food grade

leaves.note: Dominates the entire build. A compositional standard exists for this product, which is exactly why its coefficient is sourceable while the aerated-drinks one is not.

leaves.name: Pickles & preserves

host.source: No production tonnage published — cited page carries value only (~$870M, ~70% unorganised)
host.note: DOWNGRADED ON AUDIT. A '>1 mn t' figure was originally attributed to this page; re-opening it showed no tonnage at all. The value side ($870M) and the 70%-unorganised split did verify. Deriving tonnage from value gives ~460k t at typical retail prices, which conflicts with the unverified 1 mn t claim — hence the deliberately wide band.

intensity.source: No Indian compositional standard for achaar found
intensity.note: Western pickling is brine/vinegar based; Indian achaar is predominantly oil and salt cured.

adopt.source: Traditional Indian pickling does not use vinegar
adopt.note: Highest-leverage unknown in the model — see the sensitivity ranking.

price.source: Bulk domestic synthetic, below import unit value

leaves.note: Large host, but the adoption rate is both very uncertain and very low. A label study on the organised ~30% would collapse most of this uncertainty.

leaves.name: Mayonnaise & dressings

host.source: Derived from IMARC value ($455.66M, 2025) / assumed retail price
host.note: CORRECTED ON AUDIT — the build previously used $485.08M for 2024, which does not appear on the cited page; IMARC publishes 2025 = $455.66M and no 2024 figure. CONFIRMED: no tonnage is published anywhere for this market, so volume must be bought with a price assumption and inherits its error. A live example of the host_volume gap.

intensity.source: Acidified emulsion; no standard fetched for this build

adopt.source: Acidification is definitional for the category

price.source: Blend of synthetic and wine vinegar grades

leaves.note: Shows the second-order problem: when only value is published, you buy the volume with a price assumption and inherit its error.

leaves.name: Bakery & leavening

host.source: No production series fetched for this build

intensity.source: Minority of recipes; propionate is the usual mould inhibitor

leaves.note: Largest host market in the build, smallest dose. Lands near zero — host size alone predicts nothing.

leaves.name: Ready-to-eat & processed meals

host.source: No official RTE production series exists for India

intensity.source: Weighted across recipe archetypes; no published coefficient

adopt.source: Share of RTE recipes with an acidified component

leaves.note: Both host and dose are unmeasured. Structurally the least knowable F&B leaf.

leaves.name: ACV wellness / direct consumption

host.source: No separable category data; e-commerce offtake not scraped for this build

intensity.source: Product IS vinegar — ratio is definitionally 1.0

price.source: Premium mother-of-vinegar ACV retail, pack-size normalised

leaves.note: A DIRECT leaf: vinegar is the end product, so there is no host to nest inside and intensity is 1.0 by definition. Two of three inputs are T1 — but the host volume is pure assumption, so the leaf still bottoms out at T4. That is the weakest-link rule doing its job.

leaves.name: Pharma excipient / acetate buffers

intensity.source: Most pharma acetate comes from glacial acetic acid, not vinegar

leaves.note: Every input unsupported. Retained deliberately to show what a fully-unsourced leaf looks like — and to show, via the sensitivity ranking, that it does not matter to the answer.

leaves.name: Household surface cleaners

host.source: Home-care category volume not fetched for this build

adopt.source: 'Natural cleaning' remains a niche positioning in India

price.source: Comtrade EXPORT unit value — the closest proxy for bulk industrial grade

leaves.note: Priced off the export unit value rather than the import one: India exports cheap bulk vinegar and imports expensive specialty vinegar, so the two unit values bracket the real domestic price range.

host.source: No separable retail category — cleaning and culinary SKUs overlap

price.source: Comtrade export unit value, bulk grade

leaves.note: Direct leaf. Pack-size skew (5L jugs vs 250ml bottles) is the only available signal separating this from culinary white vinegar.

adopt.source: Vinegar herbicide is rare in Indian organic practice
